subject: QBR: scaling multipliers — stress test for GPU spend, batching & KV cache
messages:
From: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR prep — expected traffic profile delta and burst scenarios

Hi Olga,

We're finalizing our QBR packet and want to align on the worst-case traffic multipliers we'll use for the infra slide. Our FC-ML workloads expect a 4x daily peak on Black Friday-type traffic, but one of our product teams is arguing we should model 6x for safety given a new feature launch.

Two quick asks: 1) Can Redwood provide a recommended set of multipliers (2x, 4x, 6x) with estimated incremental GPU spend and headroom at 95th percentile utilization? 2) If we enable prefix KV caching + small-batch prioritization, what delta should we expect on per-token cost and slot contention?

Attachments: forecast_acme_aug28.csv (sample traffic)

Thanks,
J. Peters
CloudOps — Acme Analytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — expected traffic profile delta and burst scenarios

Lauren / Karthik / Vivek / Marissa —

Per J.'s note, I ran a targeted stress test over the last week to map multipliers -> GPU spend and utilization under our current slot model. Summary (high level):

- 2x baseline: +12% incremental GPU $/hr, 95th pct utilization remains ~68% with current autoscale.
- 4x baseline: +48% GPU $/hr, 95th pct utilization climbs to ~86%; batching starts to shift from continuous to queued bursts for long sequences.
- 6x stress: +115% GPU $/hr; 95th pct utilization saturates ~97% without pre-reserved slots and we see a 2.3x tail latency increase for 99th pct.

Important modifiers observed in the runs:
- KV cache (prefix cache) reduced token compute by roughly 18–24% for steady-state prompts with substantial reuse. This benefit is MODEL- and prompt-shape-dependent (for short completions it was smaller).
- Aggressive micro-batching (batch window 5–8ms) reduced per-token spend ~9% at 4x, but only if headroom exists; when GPUs are >90% utilized micro-batching increases latency variance (queued waiting).
- Reserving burst slots (dedicated capacity pool) at 10–15% of peak removes tail-latency spikes at 6x but incurs a fixed hourly reservation cost (modeled in the attached spreadsheet).

I attached the stress-run workbook (qbr-surge-model-v2.xlsx) and the KV cache benchmark PDF. Key asks for QBR slide decisions:
1) Approve an explicit burst-reservation policy: 10% reserved for premium routes / 5% for standard.
2) Approve a conservative multiplier for planning (recommend 4x for guidance, show 6x as extreme).
3) OK to include the KV cache savings as an active lever in our cost-sensitivity table (we can show a 15–20% delta on tokens for targeted prompt shapes).

Notes: the workbook has per-model rows (redwood-meduim, redwood-x, community-ggml variants) with quantization effects included. Karthik — there are some assumptions about sequence-length distributions I pulled from the July traffic sample; if you want I can re-run with the October synthetic feature-launch mix.

Next steps: Lauren, would you prefer I present the infra slides or should I hand-off to Vivek for the leadership run?

—Olga
Sr. Product Ops — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
Attachments: qbr-surge-model-v2.xlsx (workbook), kvcache-benchmarks.pdf (report)

Subject: Re: QBR prep — expected traffic profile delta and burst scenarios

Thanks, Olga — this is exactly the level of specificity we need for the exec QBR. Quick thoughts:

- Good call showing both 4x (planning) and 6x (stress) — make 4x the recommended runway in the QBR narrative and present 6x as a funded contingency with explicit reserved-cost callouts.
- I want a single slide that maps "lever -> unit economics impact" (batching window / KV cache / reservation %) with concrete $/token deltas. Can you synthesize that from the workbook?
- For the leadership run, Vivek should present the high-level tradeoffs; Olga, please own the model-level appendix in case we get technical questions.

One more ask: include a short bullet about feature-launch experiment options we can run in the next 30 days to validate the assumed 6x traffic shape (A/B traffic shadowing + synthetic burst tests).

I'll plan to slot 7 minutes for infra in the QBR deck. Thanks.

—Lauren
VP, Product

Subject: Re: QBR prep — expected traffic profile delta and burst scenarios

Nice work, Olga. A couple of technical clarifications for the appendix:

1) Can you break out the batching sensitivity by model family and sequence-length percentile (p50/p90/p99)? The cost benefit of batching collapsed for long sequences in my quick check.
2) For KV cache savings: show both the "observed" percent (what you measured) and a conservative "expected" percent for planning (we typically discount by 20% for QBR).
3) When you model reservation economics, include the blended slot utilization (reserved vs pooled) and show the break-even point (i.e., at what burst duration reservations pay for themselves).

I'll pull the latest trace summaries for the feature-launch cohort and drop them in the Drive link this afternoon. If you need a quick experiment design for A/B shadowing I can sketch one by EOD.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: QBR prep — expected traffic profile delta and burst scenarios — final deliverables and asks

Quick update & actions (finalizing before deck freeze):

- I've added the batching sensitivity table split by model family and p50/p90/p99 seq lengths in the appendix (tab: "batch-sensitivity"). Per Karthik's ask, there's an "observed" and a 20% discounted "planning" column for KV cache.
- Reservation economics: included a break-even chart (tab: "reservations") and three recommended policies:
  * Conservative: 5% reserved for standard routes, 10% for premium (lowest fixed cost)
  * Balanced: 10% reserved premium, 15% reserved burst (recommended for client SLAs)
  * Aggressive: 20% reserved across the board (highest fixed cost, minimal tail risk)
- Per Lauren: I'll synthesize a one-slide "lever -> $/token" summary. Expect it on Drive by EOD.

Action items:
1) Lauren: confirm the recommended presentation order (I propose pages: narrative -> lever slide -> stress results -> appendix).
2) Karthik: please drop the feature-launch trace summary in the Drive link (folder: /QBR/2028/infra) so I can re-run the model-mix assumption.
3) Vivek / Marissa: confirm if we want to commit to the Balanced reservation policy for the QBR ask.

I'll share the final deck + talking notes tomorrow AM. If Acme wants us to include a 6x column explicitly in their public-facing plan, J., let's sync offline — that changes the committed reserved-cost ask.

Thanks all,
—Olga
